title: God's love both precedes the gifts and follows them
source_text: XLVI. Et sic utrique facile concedent esse aliquem divinae dilectionis actum qui praecedit illa dona & virtutes, quae Scholastici designant nomine gratiae gratum facientis: quia scilicet, Deus nobis bene vult priusquam illa habeamus: & simul esse quendam actum ejusdem dilectionis quem praecedunt ejusmodi dona, nempe quia Deo sine illis non possumus placere atque ipsi probari. Talia vero dona atque virtutes hominem qui illis ornatus est formaliter Deo gratum & placentem constituunt. Juxta illud Petri Actorum decimo, In veritate comperi quod non est personarum acceptor Deus: sed in omni gente qui timet eum, & operatur justitiam, acceptus est illi.
pass_a_gloss: XLVI. And so both will easily grant that there is some act of divine love which precedes those gifts and virtues, which the Scholastics designate by the name of grace making pleasing: because namely, God wills us well before we have them: and at the same time that there is a certain act of the same love which such gifts precede, namely because without them we cannot please God and be approved by him. But such gifts and virtues formally constitute the man who is adorned with them pleasing and acceptable to God. According to that of Peter Acts tenth, In truth I have found that God is not a respecter of persons: but in every nation he who fears him, and works righteousness, is accepted by him.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLVI. So both sides will readily grant that there is an act of God's love that comes before the gifts and virtues the scholastics call grace that makes pleasing, since God wishes us well before we have them. They will also grant that there is an act of the same love that those gifts come before, since without them we cannot please God or win his approval.

Such gifts and virtues formally make the person adorned with them pleasing and acceptable to God. As Peter says in Acts 10: Truly I have found that God shows no partiality, but in every nation whoever fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.
